# Build Windows Release (Fa) — the flutter_app desktop build for
# windows-x64, zipped and attached to the release train the same way the
# macOS desktop DMGs are (build-macos.yml). Dispatched by the daily
# auto-publish `windows` leg (daily-publish.yml), which is the Windows
# counterpart of the TestFlight leg: one release-quality app build per
# day, attached to the next derived tag.
#
# The asset is fa-app-windows-x64.zip — a STABLE name (no version suffix),
# like fa-windows-x64.zip (the CLI) and fa-macos-*-mac.zip, so
# releases/latest/download/ links on fa1.dev never rot. It is NOT in
# scripts/release_required_assets.txt yet: the leg is young and a missed
# daily must not block a tag train; promote it to required once the leg
# has a green history.
#
# No signing/notarization: Windows runners cannot code-sign without a
# purchased OV cert; the zip is the unsigned open-source artifact (same
# class as the Android sideload APKs). SmartScreen may warn — the fa1.dev
# copy is the full source to build from.
#
# The app bundles no vendored-framework restore (unlike the macOS leg's
# WasmRun.xcframework): on Windows the wasm_run family resolves to the
# vendored path packages (vendor/wasm_run*), which compile from source in
# the native-assets hooks — nothing to download.
#
# Two artifacts ship:
#   fa-app-windows-x64.zip  — portable bundle (Fa.exe + dlls), the
#                             fa1.dev download button target;
#   fa-app-windows-x64.msix — sideload package (AppxManifest + makeappx
#                             + per-run self-signed cert, see
#                             scripts/msix/make_msix.ps1) with the
#                             public .cer beside it: import the cert
#                             (Trusted People), then Add-AppxPackage.
#                             Not Store-signed — a Partner Center MS
#                             Store submission is a separate track.
name: Build Windows Release (Fa)

run-name: "build-windows (create_release=${{ inputs.create_release }})"

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      version:
        description: 'Release version (e.g. v0.0.2) or "auto" to increment patch'
        default: 'auto'
      create_release:
        description: 'Create GitHub Release'
        default: true
        type: boolean

# Release builds are never preempted (issue #194 pt 5, same principle as
# ci.yml: tag/release runs must not be cancelled mid-flight).
concurrency:
  group: Build Windows Release (Fa)-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

permissions:
  # SEC-08 (#796): minimal default - release-attaching jobs grant
  # contents:write explicitly.
  contents: read

jobs:
  version:
    name: Derive version
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Same bound as the build-macos version twin (gh-1477): the fetch is
    # blobless and 20m is the seatbelt; the job only reads tags.
    timeout-minutes: 20
    permissions:
      contents: read
    outputs:
      version: ${{ steps.version.outputs.version }}
      tag: ${{ steps.version.outputs.tag }}
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          # gh-1477: this job reads ONLY `git tag` — blobless keeps full
          # tag/commit metadata without the blobs.
          fetch-depth: 0
          filter: blob:none

      - name: Derive build version
        id: version
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # Same tag math as build-macos.yml — all release children derive
          # the SAME next tag from the same latest tag, so the windows zip
          # lands on the release the CLI/macOS legs attach to. A lost race
          # on tag creation is fine: release_attach_or_create.sh uploads
          # into the winner's release.
          INPUT="${{ inputs.version }}"
          if [ -z "$INPUT" ] || [ "$INPUT" = "auto" ]; then
            LATEST=$(git tag --sort=-v:refname | grep -E '^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$' | head -1 || echo "")
            if [ -z "$LATEST" ]; then
              TAG="v0.0.1"
              echo "No previous tag found — starting at $TAG"
            else
              MAJOR=$(echo "$LATEST" | sed 's/v\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)/\1/')
              MINOR=$(echo "$LATEST" | sed 's/v\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)/\2/')
              PATCH=$(echo "$LATEST" | sed 's/v\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)/\3/')
              PATCH=$((PATCH + 1))
              TAG="v${MAJOR}.${MINOR}.${PATCH}"
              echo "Previous tag: $LATEST → auto-increment to $TAG"
            fi
          else
            TAG="$INPUT"
            [[ "$TAG" != v* ]] && TAG="v$TAG"
            echo "Using manual version: $TAG"
          fi
          VERSION_CLEAN="${TAG#v}"
          echo "version=$VERSION_CLEAN" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          echo "tag=$TAG" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT

  build-windows:
    name: Build Windows app (x64 release)
    runs-on: windows-latest
    needs: version
    timeout-minutes: 45
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      # EXACT patch pin (#1431 parity): the same SDK the nightly
      # build-release windows row and the flutter_app PR legs render and
      # build with — a floating patch re-resolves a new engine build.
      # Bump it in the same PR that reseeds anything a real engine delta
      # moved (goldens, size floors).
      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          flutter-version: '3.50.0'
          channel: stable
          cache: true

      - name: Create placeholder .env asset
        working-directory: flutter_app
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cat > .env << 'EOF'
          OPENROUTER_API_KEY=
          MODEL_ID=
          BASE_URL=
          HUGGINGFACE_TOKEN=
          EOF

      - name: Create placeholder firebase_options.dart
        shell: bash
        run: cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart

      # Shared composite action: --enforce-lockfile resolve + #726 retry +
      # skew fail-fast, identical to every other flutter_app CI leg.
      - uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get

      - name: Build Windows release
        working-directory: flutter_app
        shell: bash
        run: flutter build windows --release

      # Fail loud BEFORE the zip: a build that silently skipped the exe
      # (or landed under a renamed binary) must not ship an empty archive.
      - name: Verify build output
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          test -f flutter_app/build/windows/x64/runner/Release/Fa.exe
          test -f flutter_app/build/windows/x64/runner/Release/flutter_windows.dll

      - name: Zip the release bundle
        shell: pwsh
        run: |
          Compress-Archive -Path 'flutter_app/build/windows/x64/runner/Release/*' `
            -DestinationPath 'fa-app-windows-x64.zip' -Force
          Get-Item fa-app-windows-x64.zip | Select-Object Name, Length

      # MSIX sideload package (gh-2140 follow-up): same bundle, AppxManifest
      # assembled + packed with the Windows SDK's makeappx, signed with a
      # per-run self-signed cert. NOT Store-signed — the .cer ships beside
      # it and the user imports it (Trusted People) before Add-AppxPackage.
      # The version needs a 4-part form (x.y.z.0).
      - name: Build MSIX sideload package
        shell: pwsh
        env:
          APP_VERSION: ${{ needs.version.outputs.version }}
        run: |
          $v = $env:APP_VERSION
          $parts = $v.Split('.')
          while ($parts.Count -lt 4) { $parts += '0' }
          $msixVersion = ($parts[0..3] -join '.')
          powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass `
            -File scripts/msix/make_msix.ps1 `
            -BuildDir 'flutter_app/build/windows/x64/runner/Release' `
            -Version $msixVersion `
            -OutMsix 'fa-app-windows-x64.msix' `
            -CerPath 'fa-app-windows.cer'

      - name: Upload build artifact
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        with:
          name: fa-app-windows-x64
          path: fa-app-windows-x64.zip
          if-no-files-found: error

      - name: Upload MSIX artifact
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        with:
          name: fa-app-windows-x64-msix
          path: |
            fa-app-windows-x64.msix
            fa-app-windows.cer
          if-no-files-found: error

  release:
    name: Attach to release
    if: inputs.create_release
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [version, build-windows]
    timeout-minutes: 20
    permissions:
      contents: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        # scripts/release_attach_or_create.sh + release_draft_guard.sh
        # come from the repo.

      - name: Download build artifact
        uses: actions/download-artifact@9000827ccba6bdab643e8b6fd33ac0654aef8333 # v8.0.2
        with:
          name: fa-app-windows-x64
          path: asset

      - name: Attach to the release
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          # PAT (not the job token) so the tag push fires tag CI — same
          # contract as the build-macos attach (release_attach_or_create.sh
          # builds its push URL only when GH_TOKEN is set).
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_PAT }}
          RELEASE_TAG: ${{ needs.version.outputs.tag }}
          # gh-2050 policy (same as the macOS desktop attach): this is the
          # daily NEXT-TAG-DRAFT pre-stager — when the sibling train
          # publishes the derived tag while this leg is still running, the
          # gate's PUBLISHED refusal would red this leg daily. The env
          # turns that verdict into a loud whole-call skip; the next daily
          # leg pre-stages the next version's draft with fresh assets.
          RELEASE_GATE_PUBLISHED_SKIP: '1'
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          ls -la asset/
          bash scripts/release_attach_or_create.sh "$RELEASE_TAG" asset/fa-app-windows-x64.zip

      - name: Download MSIX artifact
        uses: actions/download-artifact@9000827ccba6bdab643e8b6fd33ac0654aef8333 # v8.0.2
        with:
          name: fa-app-windows-x64-msix
          path: msix-asset

      # The MSIX + its self-signed public cert ride the same release —
      # a sideload user needs BOTH files (import the .cer, then
      # Add-AppxPackage the .msix).
      - name: Attach MSIX to the release
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_PAT }}
          RELEASE_TAG: ${{ needs.version.outputs.tag }}
          RELEASE_GATE_PUBLISHED_SKIP: '1'
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          ls -la msix-asset/
          bash scripts/release_attach_or_create.sh "$RELEASE_TAG" msix-asset/fa-app-windows-x64.msix msix-asset/fa-app-windows.cer

      # Draft lifecycle invariant (issue #282): a failed/cancelled run
      # must delete its draft, never orphan it. Ownership-scoped: the
      # guard deletes only a draft whose body carries THIS run+job's
      # marker.
      - name: Draft lifecycle guard (delete orphaned draft on failure)
        if: always() && job.status != 'success'
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_PAT }}
          RELEASE_TAG: ${{ needs.version.outputs.tag }}
        run: bash scripts/release_draft_guard.sh "$RELEASE_TAG"

# Build a signed MSIX from a Windows Flutter app bundle.
#
# Usage:
#   pwsh scripts/msix/make_msix.ps1 -BuildDir <dir-with-Fa.exe> `
#     -Version 1.2.3.0 -OutMsix fa-app-windows-x64.msix `
#     -CerPath fa-app-windows.cer [-PfxPassword fa-msix]
#
# Produces:
#   -OutMsix : the signed .msix package
#   -CerPath : the self-signed public certificate the user must import
#              (Trusted People) before Add-AppxPackage — the package is
#              NOT Store-signed; this is the sideload artifact.
#
# The manifest is assembled here (no package:msix dependency — the CI
# windows runners already ship the Windows SDK that carries makeappx and
# signtool, and keeping the pack steps in-repo keeps the identity,
# version stamping and signing explicit and reviewable).
param(
  [Parameter(Mandatory = $true)][string] $BuildDir,
  [Parameter(Mandatory = $true)][string] $Version,
  [Parameter(Mandatory = $true)][string] $OutMsix,
  [Parameter(Mandatory = $true)][string] $CerPath,
  [string] $PfxPassword = 'fa-msix',
  [string] $IdentityName = 'dev.fa1.app.Fa',
  [string] $DisplayName = 'Fa'
)

$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'

$kitRoot = 'C:\Program Files (x86)\Windows Kits\10\bin'
$makeappx = Get-ChildItem $kitRoot -Recurse -Filter makeappx.exe -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
  Where-Object { $_.DirectoryName -like '*\x64' } |
  Sort-Object FullName -Descending | Select-Object -First 1 -ExpandProperty FullName
$signtool = Get-ChildItem $kitRoot -Recurse -Filter signtool.exe -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
  Where-Object { $_.DirectoryName -like '*\x64' } |
  Sort-Object FullName -Descending | Select-Object -First 1 -ExpandProperty FullName
if (-not $makeappx) { throw 'makeappx.exe not found under Windows Kits' }
if (-not $signtool) { throw 'signtool.exe not found under Windows Kits' }

$scriptDir = Split-Path -Parent $MyInvocation.MyCommand.Path
$assetsDir = Join-Path $scriptDir 'assets'

$stage = Join-Path $env:TEMP ('fa-msix-' + [guid]::NewGuid().ToString('N'))
New-Item -ItemType Directory $stage | Out-Null
try {
  # Bundle content
  Copy-Item (Join-Path $BuildDir '*') $stage -Recurse -Force

  # Logo assets (committed PNGs — see scripts/msix/assets/)
  $logoDir = Join-Path $stage 'assets'
  New-Item -ItemType Directory $logoDir | Out-Null
  foreach ($a in 'Square44x44Logo.png', 'Square150x150Logo.png', 'StoreLogo.png') {
    Copy-Item (Join-Path $assetsDir $a) $logoDir -Force
  }

  $escapedName = [System.Security.SecurityElement]::Escape($DisplayName)
  $manifest = @"
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<Package
  xmlns="http://schemas.microsoft.com/appx/manifest/foundation/windows10"
  xmlns:uap="http://schemas.microsoft.com/appx/manifest/uap/windows10"
  xmlns:rescap="http://schemas.microsoft.com/appx/manifest/foundation/windows10/restrictedcapabilities">
  <Identity Name="$IdentityName" Version="$Version" ProcessorArchitecture="x64" Publisher="CN=fa1.dev, O=Fa" />
  <Properties>
    <DisplayName>$escapedName</DisplayName>
    <PublisherDisplayName>Fa (fa1.dev)</PublisherDisplayName>
    <Logo>assets\StoreLogo.png</Logo>
  </Properties>
  <Dependencies>
    <TargetDeviceFamily Name="Windows.Desktop" MinVersion="10.0.17763.0" MaxVersionTested="10.0.26100.0" />
  </Dependencies>
  <Resources>
    <Resource Language="en-us" />
  </Resources>
  <Applications>
    <Application Id="Fa" Executable="Fa.exe" EntryPoint="Windows.FullTrustApplication">
      <uap:VisualElements
        DisplayName="$escapedName"
        Description="Fa — cross-platform AI coding agent (flutter_agent_harness desktop app)"
        BackgroundColor="transparent"
        Square150x150Logo="assets\Square150x150Logo.png"
        Square44x44Logo="assets\Square44x44Logo.png">
        <uap:DefaultTile Wide310x150Logo="assets\Square150x150Logo.png" />
      </uap:VisualElements>
    </Application>
  </Applications>
  <Capabilities>
    <rescap:Capability Name="runFullTrust" />
  </Capabilities>
</Package>
"@
  [System.IO.File]::WriteAllText((Join-Path $stage 'AppxManifest.xml'), $manifest)

  # Pack
  & $makeappx pack /o /d $stage /p $OutMsix 2>&1 | Out-Null
  if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw "makeappx failed ($LASTEXITCODE)" }

  # Self-signed cert (per-run) + sign
  $existing = Get-ChildItem 'Cert:\CurrentUser\My' |
    Where-Object { $_.FriendlyName -eq 'Fa MSIX (self-signed)' } |
    Sort-Object NotAfter -Descending | Select-Object -First 1
  $cert = if ($existing) {
    $existing
  } else {
    New-SelfSignedCertificate -Type CodeSigningCert `
      -Subject 'CN=fa1.dev, O=Fa' `
      -KeyUsage DigitalSignature -FriendlyName 'Fa MSIX (self-signed)' `
      -CertStoreLocation 'Cert:\CurrentUser\My' -NotAfter (Get-Date).AddYears(3)
  }
  $pfx = Join-Path $env:TEMP 'fa-msix.pfx'
  $secret = ConvertTo-SecureString -String $PfxPassword -Force -AsPlainText

  Export-Certificate -Cert $cert -FilePath $CerPath | Out-Null

  & $signtool sign /fd SHA256 /f $pfx /p $PfxPassword $OutMsix 2>&1 | Out-Null

  "msix written: $OutMsix ($([math]::Round((Get-Item $OutMsix).Length / 1MB, 1)) MB)"
  "cer  written: $CerPath"
} finally {
  Remove-Item -Recurse -Force $stage -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
  Remove-Item -Force (Join-Path $env:TEMP 'fa-msix.pfx') -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
}

When you use a wildcard, matching directories are included with their contents recursively"? I believe Compress-Archive includes directory trees recursively by default (it enumerates children recursively). Yes — Compress-Archive recurses into subdirectories of matching paths. The Flutter Release bundle has top-level files (Fa.exe, flutter_windows.dll, *.dll) and subdirectories (data/, plugins/?) — actually the Windows Flutter bundle: Release\Fa.exe, Release\flutter_windows.dll, and Release\data\ (icudtl.dat, app.so, flutter_assets). Description says make_msix verified; the zip step is trivial but the recursion question matters. Since Compress-Archive does recurse (confirmed behavior: -Path with wildcard includes subdirectories and their contents), it's fine. I'm quite sure Compress-Archive recurses directories. OK.

For typed boolean input, the expression `inputs.create_release` renders as... when dispatched via API with "true" string, GitHub coerces to boolean true → run-name renders "true". OK.

# The v1.0.680 incident: the daily build-macos train resolved a tag whose
# release was ALREADY PUBLISHED (the same-tag convergence race — the tag
# train published while the daily train's slow self-hosted legs were still
# building) and re-attached fresh fa-macos-arm64 assets ~2-3h AFTER the
# signed SHA256SUMS was attached. The manifest never re-ran, so every
# `fa update` / install.sh provenance check on the train failed for every
# macOS-arm64 user. A published release must be IMMUTABLE for `fa-*`

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Dispatch a child workflow and wait for it — NEVER kill it (gh-1903).
# Shared by every dispatching daily-publish leg.
#
# gh-1903 invariant: a child run QUEUED behind siblings on the single
# self-hosted runner (fa-m5-1) is NORMAL OPERATION, not a failure mode.
# The 2026-10-26 incident (daily run 40274465122, issue #1735) cancelled
# TWO healthy queued testflight children (~31m "queue stall" each) and
# failed a fully-built v1.0.648 release solely by killing its place in
# line. What remains here:
#   * dispatch + exact run correlation, unchanged (#343 below);
#   * a read-only wait: child state + elapsed logged every poll, sibling
#     in-progress runs logged on a diagnostic interval while the child has
#     not started — NO stall timer, NO wedge cancel, NO re-dispatch;
#   * bounds: the child's own per-job server-side timeouts (#344) and the
#     leg's timeout-minutes — nothing else;
#   * exactly ONE cancel path: when the LEG itself is terminated (leg
#     timeout, manual cancel → this script gets TERM/INT), cancel only
#     THIS leg's own NEVER-STARTED child (by the already-correlated run
#     id) so an orphaned queued run cannot publish unattended when the
#     pool revives, then fail with a diagnostic naming the child run, its
#     last observed state, and the observed pool activity. A child that
#     ever started, or already completed, is never touched.
#
# The watchdog it replaces (kept for history): #344 budgeted the watch
# (~2x historical duration) and cancelled + re-dispatched a wedged run
# once; gh-172 added a queue-stall window (no in_progress job for
# max(600, budget/8)s) for the pool-held zombie (run 39374894901). Both
# heuristics false-positive on healthy queues by construction — 31m does
# not cover the cli sibling chain's 335m worst-case on the same runner —
# and each cancel loses the queue position and restarts the clock, a
# starvation loop. Zombie handling is now: CANNOT OBSERVE ⇒ CANNOT JUDGE.
# The repo-wide `gh run list --status in_progress` probe is read-only; if

+
+      - name: Re-bake goldens

              MINOR=$(echo "$LATEST" | sed 's/v\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)/\2/')
              PATCH=$(echo "$LATEST" | sed 's/v\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)/\3/')
              PATCH=$((PATCH + 1))
              TAG="v${MAJOR}.${MINOR}.${PATCH}"
              echo "Previous tag: $LATEST → auto-increment to $TAG"
            fi
          else
            TAG="$INPUT"
            [[ "$TAG" != v* ]] && TAG="v$TAG"
            echo "Using manual version: $TAG"
          fi

# uap:VisualElements

     Feedback

      Summarize this article for me

Describes the visual aspects of the app: its default tile, logo images, text and background colors, initial screen orientation, splash screen, and lock screen tile appearance.

## Element hierarchy

**[`<Package>`](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/uwp/schemas/appxpackage/uapmanifestschema/element-f-package)**
 └─ [`<Applications>`](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/uwp/schemas/appxpackage/uapmanifestschema/element-f-applications)
 └─ [`<Application>`](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/uwp/schemas/appxpackage/uapmanifestschema/element-f-application)
 └─ **`<uap:VisualElements>`**

## Syntax

```
<uap:VisualElements
  DisplayName = 'A required string between 1 and 256 characters in length. This string is localizable.'
  Description = 'A required string between 1 and 2048 characters in length.'
  BackgroundColor = 'A required value. <!-- TODO: Add description for t:ST_Color -->'
  Square150x150Logo = 'A required string between 1 and 256 characters in length that ends with `.jpg`, `.png`, or `.jpeg` that can't contain these characters: `<`, `>`, `:`, `%`, `"`, `|`, `?`, or `*`. In this string, the `/` and `\` characters can't be the first or last characters. Also, the string can contain `/` or `\` but not both.'
  Square44x44Logo = 'A required string between 1 and 256 characters in length that ends with `.jpg`, `.png`, or `.jpeg` that can't contain these characters: `<`, `>`, `:`, `%`, `"`, `|`, `?`, or `*`. In this string, the `/` and `\` characters can't be the first or last characters. Also, the string can contain `/` or `\` but not both.'
  AppListEntry = 'An optional string that can have one of the following values: "default", or "none".' >

  <!-- Child elements -->
  uap:DefaultTile?
  uap:LockScreen?
  uap:SplashScreen?
  uap:InitialRotationPreference?

</uap:VisualElements>
```

### Key

`?` optional (zero or one)

## Attributes

|  Attribute |  Description |  Data type |  Required |  Default value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

|  **DisplayName** |  A friendly name for the app that can be displayed to users. This string is localizable; see Remarks for details. |  A string between 1 and 256 characters in length. This string is localizable. |  Yes |   |

|  **Description** |  The description of the app. This string is localizable; see Remarks for details. |  A string between 1 and 2048 characters in length. |  Yes |   |

|  **BackgroundColor** |  Specifies the background color of the app tile. See the Remarks section for color names. |  A value. |  Yes |   |

|  **Square150x150Logo** |  An image used as the app's Start Screen medium tile, and on the Task Switcher. For more info about how to specify the image in this attribute, see Remarks. |  A string between 1 and 256 characters in length that ends with `.jpg`, `.png`, or `.jpeg` that can't contain these characters: `<`, `>`, `:`, `%`, `"`, `|`, `?`, or `*`. In this string, the `/` and `\` characters can't be the first or last characters. Also, the string can contain `/` or `\` but not both. |  Yes |   |

|  **Square44x44Logo** |  An image used as the app's Start Screen small tile, and on the All Apps List. For more info about how to specify the image in this attribute, see Remarks. |  A string between 1 and 256 characters in length that ends with `.jpg`, `.png`, or `.jpeg` that can't contain these characters: `<`, `>`, `:`, `%`, `"`, `|`, `?`, or `*`. In this string, the `/` and `\` characters can't be the first or last characters. Also, the string can contain `/` or `\` but not both. |  Yes |   |

|  **AppListEntry** |  The entry in the All Apps List. Select none for entry points that do not need start menu tiles. |  An optional string that can have one of the following values: *default*, *none*. |  No |   |

## Remarks

Note

The background color specified here also applies to these items:

- The button color in any app-owned dialog boxes
- The App Description page in the Store

Note

On devices that can't be rotated, an app might be shown in that device's default orientation and the app's preferred orientation will be ignored. However, on a device with a rotation lock activated, your app's preferred rotation will still be honored.

These orientation preference choices apply to both the [splash screen](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/uwp/schemas/appxpackage/uapmanifestschema/element-uap-splashscreen) and the app UI when a new session is launched for your app. The preferences can be changed during run time through the [AutoRotationPreferences](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/uwp/api/windows.graphics.display.displayinformation.autorotationpreferences) property.

For more info on tile dimension requirements, see [Tile sizes](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/previous-versions/windows/apps/hh781198(v=win.10)).

For the **Square150x150Logo** and **Square44x44Logo** images, you can supply images of different scales so that Windows can choose the best size for the device and screen resolution. You can also supply high contrast images for accessibility and localized images to match different UI languages. This feature also allows you to localize the **DisplayName** and **Description** attributes. For more info, see the [Globalization](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/previous-versions/windows/apps/hh831183(v=win.10)) topic.

The only pin is the re-baked full-page REG golden, which pins pixels, not markup ids.

Why this matters: the CHANGELOG is shipped repo documentation — future maintainers looking for the pointer file or the markup test will find neither. The behavior itself is fine as shipped (the direct stable-name link doesn't need the pointer); the fix is to correct the entry to describe what actually ships, e.g. *"gains a Windows button linking directly to the stable `releases/latest/download/fa-app-windows-x64.zip` asset (markup pinned by the re-baked full-page golden)"* — or actually add the pointer mechanism if it was intended.

Line 83 points the wide-tile slot at the square logo:

```xml
<uap:DefaultTile Wide310x150Logo="assets\Square150x150Logo.png" />
```

`Square150x150Logo.png` is 150×150 (IHDR verified), but the slot's documented contract is a wide image — Microsoft Learn, `uap:DefaultTile` schema ([learn.microsoft.com/.../element-uap-defaulttile](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/uwp/schemas/appxpackage/uapmanifestschema/element-uap-defaulttile)): *"Wide310x150Logo — The 310x150 wide version of the logo image."*
